clue.text: Collide with b---- ref!

blocks.note: the lone letter is taken as written
an ump (umpire) is a referee

explanation.surface: A furious player is told to go and barge into the bleeping referee.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'b----' look like a censored swear word; only the B counts, and the dashes are decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into something is to knock against it, a near synonym for colliding with it.

clue.text: Nerve and audacity shown in hold-up

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve
neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: A robber displays courage and cheek during a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery, but it means a traffic delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrowing where traffic or work gets delayed, which is a hold-up.

clue.text: Men in store ordered soup

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a sequence, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Shoppers in a supermarket buy a tin of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, so it is a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Open over advisory group

blocks.note: above means over
a board is a group of advisers or directors

explanation.surface: Someone says a committee's work should be transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above board is honest and conducted openly, with nothing concealed.

clue.text: Albert bid ridiculously for garden item

indicators.note: doing something ridiculously means in a silly, disordered way, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: At an auction, Albert offers an absurd sum for a garden ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird table is a raised platform in a garden where food is put out for wild birds.

clue.text: See nothing in immorality, say

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the zero goes within the word for wickedness

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
vice is wickedness or immorality

explanation.surface: Someone claims to find nothing wrong with immoral behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an instruction to look at the construction rather than a letter; 'say' is a noun here, as in 'having a say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a say in a matter means having a voice in it, the right to express an opinion.

clue.text: Gambler, one entertained by dancer with a lurid tale

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so these pieces go inside the outer word

blocks.note: a bopper is someone dancing to pop music
a dicer is one who plays at dice
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gambler and a dancer feature together in a sensational story.
explanation.walkthrough: The gambler and the one go inside the dancer, splitting it after BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-ripper is a sensational romantic novel with scenes of seduction, so a lurid tale.

clue.text: Greek hero with Amsterdam football team

blocks.note: first meaning: a warrior of the Trojan War in Homer
second meaning: the leading Dutch football club

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek warrior lines up with a Dutch football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amsterdam club took its name from the Homeric warrior, so the two senses share a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the hero of the Iliad and to the famous football club based in Amsterdam.

clue.text: Refuse in study, and close to study

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a den is a private room for study or work
the final letter of the second study

explanation.surface: Someone is turned down, both inside the study and near it.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word appears twice: first as a room, then as letters whose end is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny is to refuse, as in denying someone a request.

clue.text: Very small container at end of quay

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
the final letter of quay

explanation.surface: A miniature shipping container sits at the far end of a dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a synonym for very small or minute.

clue.text: Movement of highly skilled people one in variety organised around Italy

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the numeral goes inside the word for a variety
going around something means enclosing it, so the word for organised wraps the country abbreviation

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a brand is a kind or variety of product
ran means managed or organised
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A talk on talented emigrants turns into a muddle about Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into two matching halves, each built the same way: a word with the letter I tucked into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain drain is the emigration of educated, talented people to other countries offering better prospects.

clue.text: Something that is easily obtained at a birthday party?

definitions.text: Something that is easily obtained at a birthday party?

blocks.note: surface reading: a thing anyone can get hold of without trouble
setter's reading: a literal slice handed round at a party, which is also the idiom for an easy task

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: at a birthday party everyone gets a slice of the birthday food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something very easy to do or get, and literally names a slice served at a party.

clue.text: Fail to win card game and become exasperated

blocks.note: failing to win is losing
patience is the British name for solitaire, the one-player card game

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps losing at cards eventually gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the British name for solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose patience is to stop tolerating something and grow irritated, i.e. exasperated.

clue.text: Failed to notice, so allowed to go unpunished?

blocks.note: first meaning: missed seeing something
second meaning: deliberately ignored or forgiven a fault

explanation.walkthrough: The 'so' makes the second sense look like a consequence of the first; it is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense covers both missing something by accident and choosing to ignore an offence.

clue.text: Opera star, one difficult to please

blocks.note: first meaning: the leading female singer in an opera company
second meaning: a temperamental, demanding person

explanation.surface: A leading soprano is notoriously hard to satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for first lady names the lead soprano and, by extension, any vain, demanding person.

clue.text: Sister deciphered runes

indicators.note: deciphering unscrambles a code, so these letters are worked out into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A nun has decoded some ancient carved inscriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' suggests a nun or sibling; in Britain a sister is also a senior hospital nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior female nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: One may be requested to stop at some stage

definitions.text: One may be requested to stop at some stage

blocks.clueFragment: One may be requested to stop at some stage
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who will be asked to cease what they are doing eventually
setter's reading: a stage is a section of a route, and passengers ring the bell asking for the next stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a point in time; it is a section of a public transport route, where passengers ask to get off.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a route ask the person at the wheel of the vehicle to halt at a particular point.

clue.text: In TV repeat, initally see sly animated cat

indicators.note: a misspelling of initially, meaning only the opening letter of the word is kept
animated means lively and moving about, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of repeat
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sly cartoon cat appears in a television rerun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated cat' reads as one phrase, but 'animated' is the anagram signal and 'cat' alone is the definition. The clue misspells 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester is the cartoon cat of Looney Tunes, forever chasing Tweety Pie.

clue.text: Fish that's gone off in basket

indicators.note: food gone off has turned bad, so these letters are spoilt into a new order
something in a basket sits inside it, so the reworked letters go within

blocks.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fish left in an angler's basket has started to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' reads as spoiled, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on 'gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large marine eel, and eels are fish.

clue.text: Stiffly formal round start of unusual Jewish festival

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
to go round something is to surround it, so the formal word encloses the selected letter

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
the first letter of unusual

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person attends an unusual religious celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' looks like a description of the festival, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Purim is the Jewish festival commemorating the deliverance of the Jews in Persia, as told in Esther.

clue.text: Taken from a disc not intended for release?

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: lifted off a vinyl disc
second meaning: said privately, not for publication

explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' suggests a record coming out; here it means publishing a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made off the record is confidential, not meant to be published or quoted.

clue.text: Beginning to toil, feeble person in river

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of toil
a weed is a weak, puny person

explanation.surface: A weakling starts to struggle while swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river flowing along the Anglo-Scottish border, famous for salmon.

clue.text: Employed American editor

blocks.note: US is short for United States, so American
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A US newspaper has hired an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' suggests hiring a person; it means put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means put into service, which is a sense of employed.

clue.text: No head for details in book

indicators.note: having no head means the top is cut off, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: facts are details or particulars

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the brain to master the details in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts is the fifth book of the New Testament, recounting the early church.

clue.text: Strange aroma, scent, here in California

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A traveller notices an odd smell in the air in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Hide in rear of quarters with family

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of quarters
kin are relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: A family takes cover at the back of their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, especially when removed for leather.

clue.text: Female after remarkably loud dress in German city

indicators.note: remarkably means in a striking, unusual way, so these letters are rearranged
one thing coming after another is placed behind it, so the abbreviation is added at the end

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman is seen in a startlingly loud outfit in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Düsseldorf is a major city on the Rhine, capital of North Rhine-Westphalia in Germany.

clue.text: Almost perfect concept

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A thinker has a nearly flawless notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion, a synonym for concept.
